digest.component_or_area: bug lifecycle – caused_by link auto-derivation on close
propositions: On bug close, auto-derive a caused_by link to a culprit ticket via git-blame of the pre-fix state (fixing-commit~1) when a strict majority (>50%) of blamed lines resolve to a single commit carrying a rebar-ticket: trailer.
The auto-derivation resolver returns None (no link) on ambiguity: no file_impact, no fixing commit, no dominant culprit, or no resolvable trailer; failure to resolve never blocks close.
A --caused-by <id> parameter at close time overrides or supplements auto-derivation; the explicit link is written via graph._links._write_link_event directly, bypassing the closed-source guard.

The auto-link writes directly to the link event store after the bug transitions to closed, using _write_link_event to avoid rejection by the source_status=='closed' guard in graph._links.add_dependency.
Library callers via transition() must be able to set caused_by on close; transition() gains a caused_by parameter threaded into transition_compute.
Documentation and tests establish the >50% single-culprit threshold, prove auto-derivation defeats the closed-source guard, and confirm ambiguous multi-commit blame draws no auto-link.
